title: Hermite Plancherel identity
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f,g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ belong to $L^2$ for the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures. Then
\[
\int f(x)g(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^n}\widehat f(\alpha)\widehat g(\alpha),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is that product measure and $\widehat f(\alpha)=\int f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$ and $\widehat g(\alpha)=\int g(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$ are the coefficients against the normalized multivariate Hermite polynomials $H_\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number.
$f$ and $g$ belong to $L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
